Article Title: Datta Meghe: Veteran BJP leader Datta Meghe passes away at 89; great loss for Vidarbha, says Gadkari
Article Text: NAGPUR: Veteran BJP leader Datta Meghe passed away on Sunday evening at the age of 89, his close aide and former Nagpur deputy mayor Raghunath Malikar said.Meghe is the father of Hingna MLA Sameer Meghe and former MLC Sagar Meghe.Datta Meghe was a four-time Congress Lok Sabha MP from Nagpur, Ramtek and Wardha and was also Rajya Sabha member between 2002 and 2008. He was part of the Sharad Pawar-led (undivided) NCP when it was formed in 1999 and was a state minister.He joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2014. He is survived by his wife, two sons, two daughters and grandchildren.Union Minister Nitin Gadkari said Meghe was a like an elder brother and the news of his passing away was heart-breaking."My heartfelt tribute to him. With Dattabhau's passing, the political and social spheres of Vidarbha have suffered a great loss. Such a leader with a generous heart, broad and pure mind, will not come again. Dattabhau's contributions to the educational and medical fields in Vidarbha are noteworthy and significant," he said.From Gadchiroli to Melghat, in the tribal areas, Meghe made utmost efforts to improve the health of tribal brethren through free medical camps, Gadkari said, adding that at Sawangi Meghe, he provided free medical treatment to the poor."To provide higher education opportunities to the youth of Vidarbha, he created educational institutions. May God grant peace to the departed soul and give strength to his family and everyone to recover from this grief," the Union minister said.
Article Summary: Datta Meghe was a four-time Congress Lok Sabha MP from Nagpur, Ramtek and Wardha. He was also Rajya Sabha member between 2002 and 2008. He is the father of Hingna MLA Sameer Meghe and former MLC Sagar Meghe.

Article Title: Drug peddler held with heroin worth Rs 1.5cr
Article Text:
.

JAMMU: Jammu Police arrested a drug peddler and seized from him around 262g heroin, worth approximately Rs 1.5 crore in the international market, along with Rs 1.5 lakh cash, a cellphone, and a weighing machine, on Saturday.A police naka team, led by PSI Rajan Choudhary, was deployed at Tutray Chowk Ring Road and spotted the suspect around 7.40pm. The accused tried to escape but was caught. Police identified him as Harpal Singh, a resident of Kathua district.Cops registered a case under NDPS Act at Miran Sahib PS. Further investigation was underway to unearth the forward and backward linkages of the nexus, police said.
Article Summary: Jammu Police arrested a drug peddler and seized from him around 262g heroin, worth approximately Rs 1.5 crore in the international market. A police naka team, led by PSI Rajan Choudhary, was deployed at Tutray Chowk Ring Road and spotted the suspect.

Article Title: Assam assembly elections: Denied ticket by BJP, minister Nandita Gorlosa joins Congress
Article Text:
Watch Assam Elections 2026: Congress Releases List Of 42 Candidates, Gaurav Gogoi To Contest From Jorhat Assam Elections 2026: Congress Releases List Of 42 Candidates, Gaurav Gogoi To Contest From Jorhat





GUWAHATI: After being denied a BJP ticket for the upcoming assembly elections, Assam cabinet minister Nandita Gorlosa joined the Congress on Sunday night.She was serving as minister for sports and youth affairs and welfare of minorities. The BJP dropped Gorlosa from its candidate list for the Haflong seat, which she currently represents, and instead fielded first-time candidate Rupali Langthasa."Nandita Gorlosa has left BJP and joined Congress," Assam Congress media department chairman Bedabrat Bora said.Assam Congress also shared a photo showing Gorlosa joining the party. The induction reportedly took place in Haflong, while her comments on the matter are still awaited.Meanwhile, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma visited Dima Hasao district on Sunday to wish Rupali well ahead of filing her nomination papers on Monday. Sarma said that 18 sitting MLAs were denied tickets and would be assigned different responsibilities after the election.
Article Summary: Assam cabinet minister Nandita Gorlosa joined the Congress on Sunday night. She was serving as minister for sports and youth affairs and welfare of minorities. The BJP dropped her from its candidate list for the Haflong seat, which she currently represents.

Article Title: Lok Sabha Speaker seeks response from 20 rebel TMC MPs on disqualification petitions
Article Text:
Rebel TMC MPs with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in June

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who are now affiliated with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), seeking their responses within seven days to disqualification petitions filed by the TMC.The disqualification petitions are currently pending before Birla.This comes after Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta on Tuesday informed the Supreme Court that the Speaker had already issued notices to the 20 MPs on the disqualification petitions filed by the TMC under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.Mehta made the submission before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant while appearing for the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the House. The bench was hearing a plea filed by senior TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee, challenging the delay in deciding the petitions seeking the disqualification of the rebels.Responding to the submission, the bench said, "It is not a question of issuing notices, it is a question of concluding the proceedings within a time frame."During the hearing, the bench indicated that it was inclined to issue notices to the respondents on Abhishek Banerjee’s writ petition.Mehta, however, submitted that there was no need to issue notices to the Speaker or his office, stating that he would appear on behalf of Birla.The TMC has accused the 20 MPs of “abandoning” the party and subsequently joining the NCPI. Abhishek Banerjee has contended that their conduct attracts disqualification under the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution.The petition names the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the House as the principal respondents and also impleads the MPs whose disqualification is being sought.The respondents are Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachana Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Md Abu Taher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Khalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs. The MPs are now affiliated with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) The disqualification petitions are currently pending before the Speaker.

Article Title: Shiv Sena’s Gurav meets BMC chief, demands disqualification of Mumbai corporator Vishakha Raut
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) corporator and former Mumbai Mayor Vishakha Raut

Mumbai:





Shiv Sena’s Priya Gurav on Tuesday met BMC chief Ashwini Bhide and demanded the disqualification of Shiv Sena (UBT) corporator and former mayor Vishakha Raut, alleging that the latter had contested the OBC-reserved ward using an invalid Kunbi caste certificate during the 2026 civic polls.In a representation to Bhide, Gurav cited an August 21 order of the Palghar District Caste Verification Committee, cancelling Raut’s OBC certificate, following a complaint alleging that it was invalid. Gurav said she had received a copy of the order via email.Gurav, daughter of former Sena MLA Sada Sarvankar, had contested the 2026 BMC polls against Raut from Ward 191 in Dadar, which was reserved for women from the OBC category, and lost. Raut had submitted an OBC certificate to establish her eligibility for the reserved seat. But last week, the Palghar committee caste scrutiny committee invalidated the OBC certificateRaut, however, had alleged that the decision was taken under political pressure from Shiv Sena. She maintained that she belongs to the OBC category and said her family’s ancestral village is in Palghar district.Raut is a corporator from the politically significant Dadar–Shivaji Park area, and had managed to retain the seat for her party by securing 13,236 votes, edging past Gurav, who polled 13,039 votes. The victory margin stood at a slender 197 votes, making it one of the tightest contests in this round of the BMC elections.This was also among those seats wherein there were only two candidates who were contesting on the seat owing to which any split in voters was unlikely.So far, four BMC corporators have been disqualified over invalid caste validity certificates: Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Deepak Sawant from Ward 111 in Bhandup, AIMIM’s Sameer Ramzan Patel from Ward 137 in Govandi, AIMIM’s Roshan Shaikh from Ward 138, and NCP’s Bushra Nadeem Malik from Ward 170 in Kurla East. All four were elected from reserved-category seats, and their memberships were terminated after the respective district caste scrutiny committees invalidated their certificates. Several of the corporators have challenged the decisions in court.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena’s Priya Gurav met BMC chief Ashwini Bhide and demanded the disqualification of Shiv Sena (UBT) corporator and former mayor Vishakha Raut. Gurav, daughter of former Sena MLA Sada Sarvankar, had contested the 2026 BMC polls against Raut from Ward 191 in Dadar, which was reserved for women. Raut had submitted an OBC certificate to establish her eligibility for the reserved seat.

Article Title: MCOCA invoked against 11 linked to illegal abortion racket for the first time in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





Police have invoked the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against 11 individuals involved in an illegal sex determination and abortion racket in Kolhapur district. This marks the first application of MCOCA for offences under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) acts, treating the operation as a sophisticated, organised criminal network.The approval to apply MCOCA was granted by Ranjan Kumar Sharma, special inspector general ofpolice (Kolhapur range), following a detailed proposal submitted by the Kolhapur police.The racket was dismantled on July 1 during a raid on a workers’ room at a sugar factory. Investigators unearthed an illegal sex determination operation allegedly conducted by individuals lacking any medical qualifications.According to the police, the accused operated a well-organised network that systematically targetted pregnant women. The group allegedly managed every stage of the crime: scouting for clients, procuring illegal sonography machines, conducting tests at clandestine locations, disclosing the sex of foetuses, and arranging illegal abortions when a female foetus was detected.Criminal records revealed that several of the accused were repeat offenders with histories of similar crimes across Kolhapur district. The decision to escalate the legal charges follows a high-level meeting on Aug 13, chaired by Shiv Sena MLC Neelam Gorhe and attended by senior police and health officials, where calls were made for tougher action against persistent violators.Police officials explained that a primary reason for invoking MCOCA is the tendency of such offenders to secure bail and promptly resume their illegal activities. By using the tougher law, authorities hope to create a lasting deterrent against rackets that contribute significantly to the state’s declining sex ratio at birth.The 11 accused currently in custody are Swapnil Patil, Mahesh Patil, Shrimant Patil, Vijay Kolaskar, Prashant Jadhav, Dattatray Patil, Omkar Karale, Sunil Patil, Anil Tipugade, Shivprasad Patil, and Ashwini Shinde.In addition to the new MCOCA charges, the group faces prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, the Maharashtra Nursing Homes Registration Act, the PCPNDT Act, and the MTP Act. The initial case was registered following a formal complaint by the taluka medical health officer.
Article Summary: Police have invoked the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against 11 individuals involved in an illegal sex determination and abortion racket in Kolhapur district. This marks the first application of MCOCA for offences under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) acts. The racket was dismantled on July 1 during a raid on a workers’ room at a sugar factory.

Article Title: Kidney racket: 2 accused withdraw bail pleas in HC
Article Text:
Nagpur:





The Nagpur bench of Bombay high court on Tuesday disposed of bail applications filed by alleged kidney-racket kingpin Ramkrishna Malleshmansanchu and Delhi-based doctor Ravindrapal Singh after their lawyers sought permission to withdraw the pleas when the court indicated it was inclined to reject them.Both are accused in a case registered under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act in connection with an alleged kidney-selling racket in Brahmapuri, Chandrapur district.The prosecution alleged that Malleshmansanchu coordinated the racket and arranged kidneys for patients requiring transplants by allegedly offering money to financially vulnerable people. Investigators alleged Singh travelled from Delhi to perform transplant surgeries.The pleas came up before Justice MM Nerlikar. Senior counsel and govt pleader Deven Chauhan represented the state and was assisted by Ujjwal Phasate, who opposed their bail pleas.After hearing both sides, the court indicated it was not inclined to grant bail. The accused then sought permission to withdraw their respective pleas, which the court allowed.Singh had earlier faced an adverse order from the Nagpur bench in a separate petition seeking quashing of the criminal case and charge sheet. The court dismissed the petition after finding that an affidavit submitted with it was fabricated and imposed a Rs 25,000 penalty.The latest proceedings concern only the bail applications and do not determine the guilt of either accused.
Article Summary: The Nagpur bench of Bombay high court disposed of bail applications filed by alleged kidney-racket kingpin Ramkrishna Malleshmansanchu and Delhi-based doctor Ravindrapal Singh. Both are accused in a case registered under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act. Investigators alleged Singh travelled from Delhi to perform transplant surgeries.

Article Title: Jalgaon police constable arrested after surrendering in murder attempt case
Article Text:
Nashik:





A suspended police constable surrendered at the Yawal police station on Sunday, after the Bombay High Court (HC) rejected his anticipatory bail application, citing his active role in a case of attempt to murder.On Mar 28 this year, a 60-year-old woman registered a complaint against him and his family members for attempt to murder, after she and her daughter were attacked with iron rods over a dispute about a gram sabha member. A complaint was registered against the Yawal police station.Soon after the complaint, senior officials took note of the allegation against the constable, and he was suspended from police service on Mar 31. He was then transferred to the Savedi police station.On the very day of his suspension, a preliminary inquiry was initiated, and the report was submitted on June 28.Following the report’s findings, the Jalgaon police finalised departmental action against him. On Aug 21, it was decided to withhold his increments for two years, said SP Shrikant Dhivare.The case was investigated by Yawal police and a chargesheet was also filed on July 30. The chargesheet mentioned that a supplementary charge sheet would be submitted upon the constable’s arrest, as he had been evading arrest.Meanwhile, with his anticipatory bail application turned down by the Bombay HC, the constable surrendered before the Yawal police station, where he was taken into custody.Further investigations are underway by the Yawal police.
Article Summary: A 60-year-old woman registered a complaint against him and his family members for attempt to murder. She and her daughter were attacked with iron rods over a dispute about a gram sabha member. The case was investigated by Yawal police and a chargesheet was also filed on July 30.

Article Title: Lady doctor arrested near Salem for illegal fetal gender determination
Article Text: SALEM: Police on Wednesday arrested a lady doctor in Vazhapadi in Salem district on charges of illegally determining and disclosing the gender of fetuses to pregnant women. Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running in the area. They sealed the clinic.Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child.Acting on a complaint, a team led by joint director Dr S P Nandhini, Attur district health officer Dr N Yoganand and Vazhapadi Government Hospital chief medical officer Dr Ramesh Kumar raided the facility.They found that Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had received Rs 30,000 from a pregnant woman to determine the gender of her fetus. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.Health department officials said this was not the first violation by the clinic. It had been raided twice earlier, and Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had faced restrictions on conducting scans and treatments, they said. Cases were registered against her then too.
Article Summary: Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running. Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.

Article Title: DYFI, YC protest Railway Board’s decision to reorganize Palakkad railway division
Article Text:
Palakkad

:





DYFI has intensified its agitation against the Railway Board’s decision to reorganize Palakkad railway division, with protests being held at major railway stations across all districts of north Kerala.DYFI activists took out marches to major railway stations in Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod districts as part of the protest. The march to Shoranur railway station on Tuesday was inaugurated by DYFI district secretary R Jayadevan.Youth Congress has also launched protests against the decision. TNN
Article Summary: DYFI activists took out marches to major railway stations in Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod districts. The march to Shoranur railway station on Tuesday was inaugurated by DYFI district secretary R Jayadevan.

Article Title: Two get five years’ imprisonment for attempting to murder homemaker
Article Text:
Idukki

:





The Idukki third additional district and sessions court has sentenced two men to five years’ imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 40,000 each for trespassing into a house and attempting to murder a woman by assaulting her. The verdict was delivered 13 years after the incident.Judge S S Seena convicted Shais, 44, of Ozhukkayil House at Mankuva in Konnathady, and Jayesh alias Chanthu, 38, of Plachery House at Munitandu in Mannamkandam, Adimali.The incident took place at a house in Pipeline area of Vellathooval village under Kunchithanny around 2am on April 24, 2013. According to the prosecution, the accused trespassed into the house and attacked the woman, a homemaker, while she was asleep in bed. The assault was allegedly carried out with the intention of killing her.Adimali police registered a case and launched an investigation. The probe was led by the then Adimali Inspector K Jinadevan. A chargesheet was subsequently filed against the accused.After considering the evidence and witness statements produced by the prosecution during the trial, the court found both accused guilty and sentenced them to jail.
Article Summary: Shais, 44, of Ozhukkayil House at Mankuva in Konnathady, and Jayesh alias Chanthu, 38, of Plachery House at Munitandu in Mannamkandam, Adimali, found guilty. The incident took place at a house in Pipeline area of Vellathooval village under Kunchithanny.
